chapter: Clarifications and portraits: Lester Young, Byas, Blanton, Ben Webster
title: Follow-ups: Marlowe Morris, Chicago leaders Dickerson, Tate, Punch Miller, Elgar, and the
summary: Short portraits of the pianist and the Chicago bandleaders; asks about a poll.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Back to Hollywood and the Streets of Paris you mention in your story about Big Sid doing the driving, Marlowe Morris was in the car. Did Marlo Morris play with you?

He was a pianist. A very good pianist. He played more on the stride type of piano playing. Using his left hand, you know. But if you had to swing, he could do that too. He could play some beautiful ballads.
He did quite a bit of recording didn't he?
Yeah.
You mentioned Carroll Dickerson real fast. What about Carroll Dickerson?
Well, Carroll was -- when I met him he

was a sort of rabble rouser. He drank and we had a club room at the musicians union. 208 in Chicago. He was always all mouth all the time, you know. If he got a gig, he would get him a bunch together. He never played, sit in front of the band and conduct it.
You mentioned Erskin Tate.
Yes, well Erskin was the violinist, but he didn't play when I worked with him. He conducted. He would just get a group together and play a gig and that was it.
That was when you were where?
In Chicago.
And you mentioned the legendary Punch Miller.
Yes.
What about him?

Well, they had a club on 43rd Street called the All Stars. Musicans used to go in there and jam a lot. And I'd go in there and I'd run into Punch. That was like home base for Punch. He wouldn't go any further than from the All Stars to play, you know, and he had recently, I hear, there is a book written on his life, you know. And his contributions to music, you know, the things that he had done that I was unaware of. And I still haven't read the book.
You say 43rd street, 43 street, where?
Chicago. Between Indiana and Michigan
Boulevard.
Elgar.
You also mentioned Charles (unintelligible)
bret)

Yes, well now, Charles was the type person, he would organize a group for a date but he was never there. He would put a band director in charge, you know. But he would do the hiring but he was one of the pet bandmen in his day, you know.
said there was
You a pool going on while Duke Ellington was first, then Fletcher, then Don Redman you were in high school, What pool was that?
Well pools, just like they hold today.
But I mean, was it a magazine that you were aware of or radio or --
Well, I forget the name of this magazine, there was one before the Tempo, Tempo was before Downbeat. But I can't remember the name of the magazine before Tempo.
